note: Set B correctly separates the gable's P3 finish from its steel L-bracket attachment, whereas Set A merges them into one misbound claim ('P3 STEEL L-BRACKET') and separately mislabels white thinset mortar as the backsplash material and 'PT1' as a surface finish. Set A also misreads 'FIN. BATHROOM FLOOR' as a subfloor condition and invents a 'finished' condition on the 3" subfloor, while B states the subfloor thickness cleanly. Both sets misbind the 3/4" MDF dimension to the edge strip (it belongs to the gable) and both invent a 'direction E' slope condition. Set B is cleaner on the core details despite more repetition of the same facts.
remarks: Both sets fabricate the quote '3/4" MDF EDGE STRIP' and '3/4" MDF GABLE' is the actual text: the 3/4" MDF dimension belongs to the gable, and the edge strip has no dimension on the page. Both also attach a 'direction E' condition to the 1/4"/ft substrate slope; the 'E' in the text layer is a grid/zone bubble, not a slope direction. Both miss the D5 LAUNDRY MILLWORK DETAIL scale (1 1/2" = 1'-0"), the waterproof membrane, blocking as req'd, thin set and line of finished countertop notes. Set B repeats several facts under two names (wallboard thickness, D1 scale, backsplash scale, glass tile dimensions, thinset adhesive) and one value is garbled as '2" x 6" "'.
